findings.title: The real-range audit run is not saved with the PR
findings.description: The PR adds the release-notes-audit skill and its tests, but no saved audit output for a real repository range is in the diff. The only evidence under `evidence/day13/` is a test run and a `check` run, and neither is an audit of a range; the skill's required `audit.txt`, `notes.json`, `group.json` and the other evidence files are absent. The PR author's notes say the fresh-session run is deferred until after the merge, so this is a planned gap rather than an oversight, but the verification criterion is still unmet at the point this PR is reviewed. Until that run is saved, the skill has only been dry-run from the drafting session, and those dry-run results are not stored as evidence.

findings.title: A skipped source change can pass the gate
findings.description: The gate procedure applies its Markdown-and-evidence-only test only when the review is for an older commit, while its MET condition accepts a completed review at the head. Qodo can record a head run as completed with `review_effort: skip` and `review_complete: false`, so a skipped head containing source or test changes can reach MET without a complete review.

findings.title: Swapped JSON sources pass the audit
findings.description: `json-links` retains only each entry's source SHA and URL, then compares SHA membership rather than the source associated with each grouped entry. Swapping the source objects of two JSON entries preserves every checked SHA and URL while making both entries attribute their subjects to the wrong commits.

findings.title: Swapped Markdown links pass the audit
findings.description: `auditNotes()` compares the SHAs extracted from Markdown entry lines with JSON entry SHAs as a collection, without checking whether each line links to its own entry. Swapping two commit links leaves that collection unchanged, so `markdown-links` reports PASS even though both subjects link to the wrong commits.

findings.title: Contradictory check totals can pass
findings.description: The audit parses `check`'s passed, failed and skipped totals but discards them, validating only its overall checked and malformed counts. A check output whose three verdict totals do not add up to the range size can therefore still produce `audit: PASS`, even though the check's own account of the history is inconsistent.

findings.title: Merge-only ranges cannot use the default
findings.description: The default audit command extracts the repository URL exclusively from the first shown JSON entry. For a non-empty range containing only ignored merges, rendering succeeds but supplies no entry, leaving the URL empty and causing the audit to exit with a bad-input error unless the operator supplies a URL separately.

findings.title: Gate reports omit finding decisions
findings.description: The gate skill's prescribed finding row omits the finding type, Qodo category, decision and evidence required by the project's gate report. Following this procedure yields a MET or NOT MET report that does not record why findings were fixed, disputed or merely reported.

findings.title: Audit can't catch a wrong link base by default
findings.description: Step 5 of the skill takes the expected repository URL from the first `commitUrl` in the `notes.json` file being audited and passes it to `audit.ts` unless `REPO_URL` is set. When `render --origin` produces the same wrong host, owner, or repository in JSON and Markdown, `json-links` and `markdown-links` only confirm that the links match that wrong base, so the audit passes after a rendering change.

findings.title: Two merges with the same short id fail the audit
findings.description: `check-agrees` compares merge commits using seven-character SHA prefixes and treats repeated skip prefixes as unexpected, even when distinct merge commits legitimately produce identical-looking skip lines. When two merge commits share a prefix, the audit reports FAIL for correct output, and a skip line can also match a different commit with that prefix.

findings.title: Reverted code bypasses review
findings.description: `pr-gate-check` uses an endpoint-to-endpoint `git diff --name-only` to decide whether the skipped-review allowance covers changes since the last complete review. If a code file changes in an intermediate commit and is reverted before the head, the diff omits it, allowing a docs-only gate result even though the allowance requires every intervening commit to be docs-only.

findings.title: Fork heads escape file checks
findings.description: `pr-gate-check` fetches only `origin` before diffing the reviewed commit against the pull request head, and gives no stop condition for a failed diff. For a fork pull request whose head object is absent locally, `git diff` fails without listing files, so the skipped-review allowance can be assessed as though no disallowed files changed.

review_agent_comment: The read-only approach is appropriate, and the audit script looks clean and aligned with the ticket. Before relying on PASS or MET as a decision, make sure the expected repository URL is independent of the rendered notes and that a completed Qodo run is not treated as a complete review. Please also tighten the skill instructions for consistency and robustness around shell usage and user-provided paths.
